## Phase 1: Context Gathering

**Context loaded**: stack=generic, 5 feature specs analyzed (systemd-unit-versioning, socket-liveness-monitoring, register-correction), 4 domain assumptions identified, 3 source documents parsed.

---

## Phase 2: Initial Proposal

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
FEATURE SPEC PROPOSAL: Jarvis Serve-NATS Watchdog
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Feature: Jarvis Serve-NATS Watchdog
  As a system operator
  I want the Slack ingress door monitored for staleness and the correct service unit versioned
  So that absent-operator failures of the Slack door are detected and alerted without self-recovery delay

  Background:
    Given the jarvis-serve-nats service is the real Slack ingress on-box
    And the service is managed as a systemd user unit

━━ GROUP A: Key Examples (3 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Core path — versioned unit file exists and matches the real service
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: Versioned systemd unit file exists for jarvis-serve-nats
    Given the service is managed as a systemd user unit
    When the operator inspects the ops/systemd directory
    Then a file named jarvis-serve-nats.service should exist
    And the unit file should match the running service configuration

  # Why: Core path — watchdog detects a quiet door and posts an alert
  @key-example @smoke
  Scenario: Watchdog posts a Slack alert when the door goes quiet
    Given the jarvis-serve-nats service has no fresh subscription activity in the last 5 minutes
    When the watchdog runs its staleness check
    Then an alert should be posted to the Slack channel
    And the alert should identify the jarvis-serve-nats service by name

  # Why: Core path — register correctly names the Slack door
  @key-example
  Scenario: O-30 register names serve-nats as the Slack door
    Given the O-30 register exists
    When the operator reviews the register
    Then the register row for Slack ingress should name serve-nats
    And the register should not reference langgraph dev as the Slack door

━━ GROUP B: Boundary Conditions (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Just-inside boundary — activity just within the quiet window prevents alert
  @boundary
  Scenario: Door with recent subscription activity does not trigger an alert
    Given the jarvis-serve-nats service had subscription activity 4 minutes ago
    And the quiet threshold is 5 minutes
    When the watchdog runs its staleness check
    Then no alert should be posted

  # Why: Just-outside boundary — activity just older than the quiet window triggers alert
  @boundary @negative
  Scenario: Door with stale subscription activity triggers an alert
    Given the jarvis-serve-nats service had subscription activity 6 minutes ago
    And the quiet threshold is 5 minutes
    When the watchdog runs its staleness check
    Then an alert should be posted

━━ GROUP C: Negative Cases (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Unauthorised or incorrect service reference must not be accepted
  @negative
  Scenario: Register referencing langgraph dev as the Slack door is rejected
    Given the O-30 register exists
    When the register contains a row naming langgraph dev as the Slack door
    Then the register should be flagged as incorrect
    And the correction should name serve-nats instead

  # Why: Watchdog must not alert when the service is healthy but has no recent activity
  @negative
  Scenario: Watchdog does not alert when the service is known to be idle but healthy
    Given the jarvis-serve-nats service is running normally
    And the service has no message traffic for 30 minutes
    When the watchdog runs its staleness check
    Then no alert should be posted
    And the service health should be confirmed from the journal

━━ GROUP D: Edge Cases (2 scenarios) ━━

  # Why: Unusual situation — unit file exists but does not match the running service
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Versioned unit file differing from the running service is detected
    Given a versioned jarvis-serve-nats.service file exists
    When the operator compares it with the running service configuration
    Then the difference should be surfaced for correction
    And the versioned file should be updated to match

  # Why: Failure recovery — watchdog cannot parse journal output
  @edge-case
  Scenario: Watchdog handles unreadable journal output without crashing
    Given the journalctl command returns no output or errors
    When the watchdog runs its staleness check
    Then the watchdog should report the journal read failure
    And the watchdog should not post a false-positive alert

Total: 9 scenarios across 4 groups
Inferred assumptions: 4 (will be resolved in Phase 5)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

## Phase 3: Human Curation

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
CURATION: Review each group
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

For each group, you may:

  [A] Accept  — include all scenarios in this group as-is
  [R] Reject  — exclude all scenarios in this group
  [M] Modify  — accept but specify changes (provide inline)
  [+] Add     — accept and add additional scenarios you describe
  [?] Defer   — mark group for future specification; excluded from output

Fast path: type "A A A A" to accept all four groups at once.

GROUP A — Key Examples (3 scenarios): _
GROUP B — Boundary Conditions (2 scenarios): _
GROUP C — Negative Cases (2 scenarios): _
GROUP D — Edge Cases (2 scenarios): _
```

---

## Phase 4: Edge Case Expansion (optional)

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
EDGE CASE EXPANSION (optional)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

I've identified 3 additional scenarios covering security, concurrency, and integration boundaries:

Security (1):
  - Watchdog does not expose journal contents or service parameters to unauthorised parties when posting alerts

Concurrency (1):
  - Multiple watchdog instances running simultaneously do not post duplicate alerts for the same staleness event

Integration boundaries (1):
  - Slack webhook endpoint is unavailable or returns an error; watchdog handles this gracefully

Include them? [Y/S/N]: 
```

---

## Phase 5: Assumption Resolution

```
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
ASSUMPTION RESOLUTION (4 items)
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━

Each assumption has a proposed default. Press Enter to accept,
or type the actual value.

[1] Quiet time window for staleness detection
    Proposed: 5 minutes  Confidence: medium  Basis: Typical Socket liveness threshold
    Accept or enter value: _

[2] Slack alert channel/webhook
    Proposed: #ops-alerts with webhook URL from env var SLACK_WEBHOOK  Confidence: low  Basis: Conventional monitoring channel
    Accept or enter value: _

[3] Journal pattern for subscription activity
    Proposed: Lines containing "NATS" or "subscribe" or "message" within the time window  Confidence: low  Basis: General NATS logging conventions
    Accept or enter value: _

[4] O-30 register location
    Proposed: docs/ops/register-o30.md  Confidence: low  Basis: Common ops documentation path
    Accept or enter value: _
━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━━
```

---

**Your input is required at Phases 3, 4, and 5.** Please review the proposal and provide your curation choices.
